transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-28
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Rachel Park (Luminary CISO), Tom Bennett (Luminary Head of Platform), Mina Shah (Luminary Infra)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment choices. Customer high-level concerns: SOC 2 and ISO evidences, SSO/SAML & SCIM provisioning, RBAC model for multi-tenant access, audit logs retention and export, encryption/KMS key management (bring-your-own-key), and data residency / retention policies. Agreed next step: send compliance artifacts and schedule a technical deep-dive.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 / ISO27001 status and evidence locations
- SSO SAML and SCIM for provisioning, SSO test accounts
- RBAC / least privilege and admin separation
- Audit logs, retention, and log forwarding to customer SIEM
- Encryption at rest/in transit, BYOK / KMS integration
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, data isolation, compliance)

Action items (recap at end): see metadata action_items

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Diego our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Rachel (Luminary): Doing good, thanks. Busy week but happy to be here.
[00:08] Tom: Same. We've been looking at Redwood for inference — mostly from a security and compliance lens.
[00:12] Samira: Awesome, that's what we want to cover today. High level, is this more of a hosted-first evaluation or are you leaning toward dedicated / private from day one?
[00:20] Rachel: We're evaluating all three. For our regulated workflows we need airtight controls — SOC2 report is a must, and ISO as well is nice to have. We've got Okta for SSO and need SAML support and SCIM provisioning.
[00:29] Diego (Redwood): Yep, Redwood supports SSO via SAML and SCIM for user provisioning; for enterprise customers we can integrate with Okta, Azure AD. We also support role-based access controls...sorry RBAC with fine-grained roles, admin separation, and audit logs.
[00:39] Mina: When you say audit logs, is that full request+response or metadata only? We can't have PII in logs.
[00:45] Diego: Good question. By default we log metadata and operational events; by policy we can capture request/response traces for debugging with redaction. For hosted, request/response storage is encrypted and access-controlled — we have policies to redact sensitive fields. For Private/Dedicated, customers can opt to forward logs to their own SIEM (we support syslog / S3 / ELK ingest).
[01:00] Rachel: And retention — what's the default retention for audit logs? We're looking at 1 year for audit trails; longer for some datasets.
[01:06] Samira: Default hosted retention is 90 days for detailed logs and 365 days for higher-level audit events; we can adjust via add-on or enterprise agreement. For Dedicated and Private you can control retention and export externally.
[01:18] Tom: KMS — we use AWS KMS and we require BYOK for certain keys. How does Redwood handle customer-managed keys?
[01:24] Diego: We support BYOK for encryption at rest. For hosted we can either use our managed keys or integrate with your AWS KMS/CloudHSM or Azure Key Vault via a secure key-wrap pattern. For Private deployments keys remain in your VPC and you control lifecycle. There's a bit of setup for rotation and access policies but we have runbooks.
[01:38] Rachel: Is that covered in SOC2 evidence? I need to show auditors how keys are controlled.
[01:42] Samira: Yes, our SOC 2 Type II report includes key management controls; we'll share the redacted report and the ISO27001 cert. We'll also include the KMS integration guide which shows how BYOK is implemented.
[01:52] Mina: Network isolation — if we do Dedicated, is there a VPC peering or private link option? We can't have any public egress for some workloads.
[01:58] Diego: For Dedicated we provide Private Link and VPC peering options; for Private deployments we can package the control plane in your VPC or on-prem. You can disable public endpoints. There are configuration steps for NAT and egress control.
[02:10] Tom: Any SOC2 or ISO caveats for hosted multi-tenant? Auditors are sometimes picky about logical separation.
[02:14] Samira: We document logical separation and tenant isolation, continuous monitoring, and encryption boundaries in our compliance pack. For customers needing stronger isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private where you get compute isolation and separate network.
[02:26] Rachel: Ok. What about RBAC integration with our existing IdP groups? We don't want to centralize roles in two places.
[02:31] Diego: We support SCIM group sync and can map IdP groups to Redwood roles (admin, developer, read-only, billing). There's also an API for role provisioning if you need more custom mapping.
[02:42] Mina: Audit trails need to include who did model rollouts and what model versions were deployed — can we get immutable logs?
[02:48] Diego: Yes, model lifecycle events are logged with user identity. We can forward them to your SIEM, and for Dedicated/Private they can be stored in your S3 with immutability policies. For hosted we can provide a tamper-evident audit export.
[02:59] Tom: Do you support PCI or HIPAA-specific controls? We're not doing PCI, but some of our partners require HIPAA assurances.
[03:05] Samira: We have customers in healthcare using Private deployments and sign BAAs where appropriate. We can discuss that in legal. Our platform controls are designed to support HIPAA compliance if deployed in Private mode with appropriate contracts.
[03:18] Rachel: One point on logs — we want to be able to correlate Redwood logs with our application logs using a trace-id. Is there a request-id we can inject?
[03:24] Diego: Yes, we can accept client-supplied request IDs that are propagated through our tracing. That makes correlation straightforward.
[03:30] Rachel: Great. A small nit: how do you handle model caching — could cached prompts be considered retention of user data? If we cache across customers that's a problem.
[03:38] Diego: Our caching is configurable per-tenant. For multi-tenant hosted customers we default to isolated caches; you can disable caching for sensitive endpoints. And KV cache does not persist PII unless configured. We'll include the caching policy doc.
[03:49] Tom: Are there any live customers in healthcare or finance we can reference for compliance?
[03:53] Samira: We can provide references after NDA; we've got several financial and healthcare customers on Dedicated/Private. We'll include anonymized references and a brief case study.
[04:02] Mina: About data residency — can hosted instances be pinned to region? We need EU-only for some data.
[04:07] Diego: Yes, we run region-specific hosted endpoints. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated in-region or Private. Our control plane can be region-aware and data storage can be pinned.
[04:16] Rachel: On the legal side, what about data retention policy and deletion requests? We need to demonstrate ability to delete data on demand.
[04:22] Samira: We support data deletion requests; for hosted we can delete customer logs and cached content within a defined SLA (usually 30 days for full purge), for Dedicated and Private you control retention and deletion. We'll share the deletion workflow and certificate of deletion process.
[04:35] Tom: Performance wise — if we go Private on-prem, how heavy is the infra footprint? We don't want to manage a whole fleet.
[04:40] Diego: Our private package varies by model family. For 13B-class models you can run on modest GPU counts; for high throughput you'd need bigger clusters. We typically size based on your QPS and latency SLOs; we can run a pilot with smaller capacity. We'll share sizing guidance.
[04:55] Rachel: One last auditor question: does Redwood rotate keys automatically or do we control rotation for BYOK?
[04:59] Diego: For managed keys Redwood rotates per our schedule; for BYOK you control rotation. We provide rotation guides and automation hooks.
[05:06] Samira: Ok, to recap next steps: I'll send SOC2 + ISO artifacts and the compliance pack; Diego will prepare KMS integration notes and a sample config, and we'll schedule a deeper technical session focusing on KMS, audit log forwarding, and RBAC mapping. Mina will share a sample traffic profile.
[05:20] Rachel: That sounds good. Can we get an estimate for cost of Dedicated pool for ~200 QPS?
[05:25] Samira: We'll include a rough estimate in the follow-up and a formal quote after the technical deep-dive.
[05:30] Tom: Thanks, appreciate it.
[05:33] Samira: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts by early next week.

End of transcript.
